pu2-ch4.title: Mendel's Experiments
pts: Gregor Mendel (1856–1863): hybridisation experiments on garden pea, Pisum sativum
Used true-breeding lines and 7 pairs of contrasting traits (tall/dwarf, round/wrinkled, yellow/green…)
Large samples + statistical analysis: the first to apply mathematics to biology
Why pea: short life span, self-pollinating, easy to cross, many clear contrasting traits
Terms: gene (factor), alleles, homozygous (TT, tt), heterozygous (Tt), genotype vs phenotype

pu2-ch4.title: Monohybrid Cross & Two Laws
pts: Tall (TT) × dwarf (tt) → F<sub>1</sub> all tall (Tt)
F2 phenotypic ratio 3 : 1 · genotypic ratio 1 : 2 : 1
Law of Dominance: in a heterozygote one allele is expressed, the other is masked
Law of Segregation: alleles separate at gamete formation, each gamete gets one (purity of gametes)
Punnett square (Reginald C. Punnett) shows gametes and all possible offspring

pu2-ch4.title: Test Cross & Deviations
pts: Test cross: dominant phenotype × homozygous recessive → 1 : 1 (if Tt) or all dominant (if TT)
Incomplete dominance: snapdragon (Antirrhinum) RR red × rr white → Rr pink; F2 1 : 2 : 1
Co-dominance: ABO blood group, IA and IB both expressed in group AB
Multiple alleles: gene I has 3 alleles (IA, IB, i) → 6 genotypes, 4 phenotypes
Pea starch grains: BB large, bb small, Bb intermediate → dominance depends on the trait studied

pu2-ch4.title: Dihybrid Cross
pts: Round yellow (RRYY) × wrinkled green (rryy) → F<sub>1</sub> RrYy, round yellow
F2 phenotypic ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 from 16 gamete combinations
Law of Independent Assortment: one pair of traits segregates independently of the other
Dihybrid test cross (RrYy × rryy) → 1 : 1 : 1 : 1
Mendel's work (1865) rediscovered in 1900 by de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak

pu2-ch4.title: Chromosomal Theory & Linkage
pts: Sutton & Boveri: chromosomes pair and segregate like Mendel's factors → chromosomal theory of inheritance
T. H. Morgan worked on Drosophila melanogaster: short life cycle, many offspring, clear variations
Linkage: genes on one chromosome are inherited together; recombination gives new combinations
Tightly linked genes recombine less: white–yellow 1.3% vs white–miniature 37.2%
Sturtevant used recombination frequency to map genes on chromosomes

pu2-ch4.title: Sex Determination
pts: Henking (1891) saw the 'X body' in insect sperm
XO (grasshopper): male XO, female XX
XY (humans, Drosophila): male heterogametic · father's sperm decides the child's sex
ZW (birds): female heterogametic ZW, male ZZ
Honey bee haplodiploidy: fertilised egg → female (2n = 32), unfertilised → male drone (n = 16)

pu2-ch4.title: Mutation & Pedigree Analysis
pts: Mutation: change in the DNA sequence → change in genotype and phenotype
Point mutation: one base changed (sickle-cell anaemia) · frameshift: bases inserted or deleted
Mutagens: UV radiation and some chemicals
Pleiotropy: one gene, many effects, e.g. phenylketonuria
Pedigree analysis traces a trait through generations with standard symbols

pu2-ch4.title: Genetic Disorders
pts: Haemophilia: X-linked recessive, blood fails to clot (Queen Victoria's family)
Sickle-cell anaemia: autosomal recessive, GAG → GUG, Glu → Val at 6th position of β-globin
Colour blindness: X-linked recessive, red–green; ~8% of males, 0.4% of females
Phenylketonuria: autosomal recessive, no phenylalanine hydroxylase · Thalassemia: autosomal recessive
Chromosomal: Down's (trisomy 21), Klinefelter's (XXY), Turner's (XO)

pu2-ch9.title: Principles of Biotechnology
pts: EFB: integration of natural science and organisms, cells, parts thereof and molecular analogues for products and services
Two core techniques: genetic engineering (alter DNA/RNA) + bioprocess engineering (sterile, large scale)
First rDNA: Cohen & Boyer (1972), antibiotic-resistance gene in a plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium
Steps: identify DNA with the desirable gene → introduce into host → maintain it and pass to progeny
A DNA piece replicates in the host only when linked to an origin of replication (ori)

pu2-ch9.title: Restriction Enzymes
pts: 'Molecular scissors'; the first one: Hind II, cuts at a specific 6-bp sequence
Naming EcoRI: E = Escherichia, co = coli, R = strain RY13, I = first enzyme isolated
Recognise palindromes, e.g. 5′-GAATTC-3′ reads the same on both strands
Cut a little away from the centre → sticky ends joined by DNA ligase
Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends · endonucleases cut within the DNA

pu2-ch9.title: Gel Electrophoresis
pts: Separates DNA fragments by size through an agarose gel (from sea weeds)
DNA is negatively charged → moves towards the anode
Smaller fragments move farther (sieving effect)
Stain with ethidium bromide + UV light → bright orange bands
Elution: bands are cut out and the DNA extracted to build recombinant DNA

pu2-ch9.title: Cloning Vectors · pBR322
pts: Plasmids and bacteriophages replicate independently; ori controls the copy number
Needs: ori, a selectable marker, and a single recognition site per enzyme (cloning site)
pBR322: ori, rop, ampR, tetR; sites BamHI, SalI, PstI, PvuI, ClaI, EcoRI, HindIII
Insertional inactivation: insert at BamHI in tetR → recombinants lose tetracycline resistance
β-galactosidase marker: recombinants give colourless colonies, non-recombinants blue

pu2-ch9.title: Vectors & Competent Hosts
pts: Agrobacterium tumefaciens Ti plasmid, disarmed → vector for plant cells
Disarmed retroviruses → vectors for animal cells
Competent cells: divalent cations (Ca2+) + heat shock (ice → 42 °C → ice)
Micro-injection: rDNA injected straight into the nucleus of an animal cell
Biolistics (gene gun): gold or tungsten particles coated with DNA, fired into plant cells

pu2-ch9.title: Processes of rDNA Technology
pts: Break cells: lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant), chitinase (fungus)
Remove RNA (ribonuclease) and proteins (protease); chilled ethanol precipitates DNA as threads
Cut with a restriction enzyme; check the digestion on an agarose gel
Join the gene to the vector with DNA ligase → recombinant DNA
Transfer into the host and pick transformants on antibiotic medium

pu2-ch9.title: Polymerase Chain Reaction
pts: PCR makes many copies of a gene of interest in vitro (~1 billion copies)
Each cycle: denaturation (high temperature) → annealing of 2 primers → extension
Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus: stays active at high temperature
Needs template DNA, two primers, dNTPs and a thermostable DNA polymerase
The amplified fragment is ligated with a vector for cloning

pu2-ch9.title: Bioreactors & Downstream Processing
pts: Bioreactors: 100–1000 litre vessels with optimum temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins, O2
Stirred-tank: agitator, oxygen delivery, foam control, temperature & pH control, sampling ports
Sparged stirred-tank: air bubbles raise the area for oxygen transfer
Continuous culture: used medium drained, fresh added → cells stay in log phase, more biomass
Downstream processing: separation, purification, formulation, clinical trials, quality control
